My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. I know this soil and this climate — cold dry winters, hot wet summers, the North China Plain rhythm. At my age, I can't do as much heavy work as before, my son is in Shijiazhuang working, so I rely on the machinery contractor (农机手) for sowing and harvest. I manage my 7 mu the same way I have for 30 years.

I will plant winter wheat on all 7 mu in October, same as always. That's the money crop. I'll buy improved seed from the township supply co-op — I stopped saving my own seed years ago, the co-op seed yields better. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer (复合肥) as base dressing and then urea at jointing. I water three times: the winter moisture irrigation (越冬水), the jointing water (拔节水), and the grain-filling water (灌浆水). I spray herbicide in November and fungicide before heading. I've been doing this exactly this way for decades. My yield is around 450 jin per mu most years — that's 450 kg, which is decent.

After wheat harvest in June, I immediately plant summer maize on the same 7 mu. The machinery plows and sows in one pass. Maize is easier — the summer rains help, I only irrigate once if July is dry. I apply urea twice, once at emergence and once at tasseling. One herbicide spray early, maybe one insecticide if the corn borer (玉米螟) is bad that year. Hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever the seed shop has. Yield around 550 kg per mu.

I also keep a small vegetable plot of half a mu near the house — garlic, Chinese cabbage, beans — but that's just for eating, I don't count it as a cash crop.
